quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You may honk your horn when you:
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to a dangerous situation.

questions.question: This sign means that:

options.text: A community group is picking up trash on the highway ahead.
Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that workers may be on or near the road. Drive carefully through this area.

questions.question: The best way to deal with tailgaters is to:

options.text: Speed up to make more distance between you and them.
Brake hard to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Watch your mirrors often to spot tailgaters. If a car follows too closely, slow down gradually and let it pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road. You should:

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force your vehicle back on the road.
Speed up and steer back on the road gradually.
Brake gently and turn the steering wheel to return to the road at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake gently and turn the steering wheel to return to the road at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: If your wheels leave the road, keep them off the pavement and slow down using gentle brake pressure. Once you reach a safe speed, turn the steering wheel to get back on the road. Do not jerk the steering wheel sharply.

questions.question: On a slippery road, the first thing you should do to slow down is:

options.text: Take your foot off the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: To slow down on a slippery road, first take your foot off the gas. If you need to slow more, apply gentle, steady pressure to the brake pedal.

questions.question: Which of the following does not happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance becomes wrong.
You stay calm and focus better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You stay calm and focus better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, hurts your vision, changes how you judge speed and distance, reduces your ability to handle headlight glare, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: What can you do to avoid making emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance behind other cars.
Drive only in the right lane.
Drive slower than the traffic flow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance behind other cars.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance gives you time to react to problems without sudden braking. This protects you and the driver behind you.

questions.question: Pedestrians in crosswalks and at intersections always have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way when crossing at an intersection. A crosswalk exists at any intersection, whether it is marked or not.

questions.question: A driver who goes much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Should not let other cars pass.
May create a dangerous driving situation.

questions.correctAnswerText: May create a dangerous driving situation.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than traffic can be unsafe. On two-lane roads, if traffic backs up behind you, pull over and let cars pass. Only drive much slower than the limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen when a driver does not see another vehicle or does something unexpected. Communicate with other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: An octagonal sign is always a:
questions.explanation: Octagonal signs are always stop signs. Stop completely when you see a red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: Drivers should be careful when passing large vehicles. You should not drive beside large vehicles for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have large blind spots on both sides. Do not drive beside a large vehicle for long. It is safer to drop back or move ahead.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic light means a ____ light will appear soon.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light will appear next.

questions.question: You are on a two-lane road with no bike lanes. A bicyclist is ahead going the same direction. What is the safest way to pass?

options.text: Slow down and wait for oncoming traffic to clear. Then pass the bicyclist with enough space between you.
Keep driving straight. The bicyclist must get out of your way.
Do not pass until you reach a traffic light or stop sign.
Honk to warn the bicyclist that you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait for oncoming traffic to clear. Then pass the bicyclist with enough space between you.
questions.explanation: Pass a bicyclist like any other vehicle. Leave at least 3 feet of space between your mirror and the bicyclist. On higher speed roads or with groups of bicyclists, leave at least 5 feet. Unnecessary honking may startle the rider and cause a crash.

questions.question: You notice a problem with your vehicle that may affect safe driving. You should:

options.text: Fix the problem as soon as possible.
Fix the problem when you have money.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix the problem as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Fix any problem that affects safe driving right away. Do not drive the vehicle until it is fixed.

questions.question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes to the left, you should look:
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot.

questions.question: Taking drugs with alcohol:

options.text: Is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
Reduces the effects of alcohol on driving.

questions.explanation: Drugs (including illegal, prescription, and over-the-counter medicines) affect your brain and driving ability. Mixing alcohol with drugs increases crash risk.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Fines double in a work zone.

questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns of low clearance ahead.

questions.question: An oncoming car is on your left and a bicyclist is on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Let the car pass, then pass the bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass, then pass the bicyclist.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first. Then pass the bicyclist. Do not try to squeeze between both at once.

questions.question: When approaching a flashing yellow light, you should:
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard. Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: How can you help prevent crashes?

options.text: Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.

questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers do unexpected things. Communicate with other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians. Use your turn signals when slowing down, stopping, or turning. Use your emergency lights or horn when needed.

questions.question: Can drivers park in handicap parking access aisles next to handicap parking stalls?
questions.explanation: No one can park in handicap parking access aisles. These aisles provide space for wheelchairs and wheelchair lifts.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to hazards ahead. This sign warns you that a T intersection is coming. Be ready to turn left or right.

questions.question: When may you pass another vehicle?

options.text: In a curve or on a hill because the chance is small that another vehicle is coming.
By using the shoulder of the highway.
If your lane is next to a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear ahead.

questions.explanation: Do not pass on a hill or in a curve because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Do not pass by driving on the shoulder. Do not pass by crossing a solid yellow line.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians at any intersection without a traffic light, with or without a crosswalk.
